2. Briefly, the facts of the case are, that, the case holding No. U/23, Block-D, Noorjahan Road Mohammadpur, Dhaka under Layout Plan No. 127/1961-62 dated 20-7-1961 had originally belonged to the erstwhile Government of East Pakistan and the same was leased out, to one A. Rafique, by a, registered\case deed being No. 9256 (Page Nos. 221-225 Volume No. 100, Book No.1 of Dhaka Sadar Sub-Registry Office) and the possession there of also delivered in favour of the said original allottee A Rafique by virtue of letter No. 7915/1(1) dated 5-10-1961 and he paid the full costs of the house. Before liberation of Bangladesh he got a clearance certificate from the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate Dhaka on 2-9-1969 vide Memo No. 166-A/O Since then he was in possession of the case property. The original allottee A. Rafique started to construct a two-storied building on the case property in the year 1969 but he could not complete the same for financial crisis for which he had no option but to sell out the suit property and made an agreement with the petitioner on 25-1-1971 and received Taka 15,000 as advance out of total consideration amount of Taka 30,000 and both the parties agreed that the Kabala will be executed arid registered on payment of Taka 15,000 to be paid within 30 days from the date of intimation by original lessee A Rafique who was supposed to execute the same after obtaining income tax certificate and other necessary papers and also to hand over the physical possession of the case property in favour of the petitioner. Subsequently, said lessee A. Rafique received Taka 10,000 from the petitioner endorsing the same in writing on the back page of the said deed of agreement Havins no response from the said A Rafique for a long period petitioner approached to execute and register the sale deed in respect of the case property which was refused by the said A Rafique; consequently the petitioner was compelled to file Title Suit No. 927 of 1981 before the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court Dhaka for specific performance of contract making the said A Rafique as defendant, wherein Government of Bangladesh was also a party. Summons were duly served upon all the parties in accordance with law and the said original lessee A Rafique duly appeared before the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka and filed written statement on 22-4-1982, ultimately the said Title Suit No. 927 of 1981 was decreed ex parte on 4-12-1983. Thereafter the petitioner by depositing Taka 5,000 to execute and register the sale deed and in compliance of the decree the petitioner got the deed of sale executed and registered vide deed No. 2433; dated 5-9-1991 and accordingly, the same was executed and registered by the said court. The petitioner has been in physical possession of the case property from its original owner since from bainapatra and before the commencement of President's Order 16 of 1972 and the physical possession of the said property has never been taken over by the Government. The petitioner subsequently came to know that the case property has been declared as abandoned property and published in the official Gazette on 23-9-1986 in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property. Finding no other alternative, the petitioner filed an application under section 7(1) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 before the Court of Settlement and appeared regularly in the said Court. But for the time being the court was not continuing due to the quorum of the court. Subsequently, the court was resumed and without giving any notice to the petitioner the Court of Settlement rejected the application by his judgment and order dated 22-7-1995. 

 4. Mr MA Quddus Sheikh, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the property in question has never been taken over by the Government and no notice was issued or served to hand over possession of the same to the authority but the said property was most illegally included in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property by violating the mandatory provision of law. He further submits that the petitioner filed application before the Court of Settlement and the notice was duly served upon the parties but subsequently, the court was not in session/operation due to the quorum and constitution of the court and thereafter, when the court was reconstituted and was resumed on 20-7-1995 no intimation was given and on the next day the Court of Settlement, without giving the petitioner an opportunity of being heard, rejected the application which is illegal, without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. He further submits that though the petitioner earlier received notice and accordingly, appeared before the Court of Settlement regularly, taken all steps in accordance with law but due to the quorum of the constitution of the Court the Court of Settlement was not in session for a long period and when the Court was reconstituted and resumed, in such event provisions of transfer of court is to be observed and, in such situation, fresh notice to the parties are to be served. In support of his submission, he referred section 10 of the Ordinance 54 of 1985 and submits that to consider the application, the Court of Settlement shall follow the provisions as laid down in the Civil Procedure Code and accordingly, summons to the parties are to be served and examining the witnesses but Court of Settlement, without giving any opportunity of being heard, disposed of the matter. He further submits that according to section 24A, summons to be served to the parties and fixing a day for appearance of the parties before it and in the instant case, the court after resumption of Its constitution/quorum did not issue any notice upon the petitioner and, as such, the petitioner could not appear and produce the documents before the Court of Settlement which is a violation of the principle of natural justice and thus, the judgment of the Court of Settlement is illegal and without jurisdiction. He further submits that the Court of Settlement opined that the case is barred by 135 days which is miscalculation of the date of filing. He further submits that the petitioner filed the application before the Court of Settlement in time and the court itself mentioned that the case was filed on 8-1-87 where the Gazette was published on 23-9-1986 and thus the statutory period of 108 days ended on 9-1-87 but the Court of Settlement miscalculated that the petitioner filed the application after 135 days which amounts to misapplication of facts and, as such the said finding is not sustainable in law and liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his argument, he referred several cited cases reported in 53 DLR (AD) 99, 57 DLR (AD) 97, 56 DLR (AD) 101 and 48 DLR (AD) 13. 

 5. Mr Md Mozammel Huq, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the Court of Settlement after considering the evidence on record opined that the case property has been rightly listed in the "Ka" list of abandoned buildings after observing all the formalities by the authority. He further submits that Court of Settlement decided the matter on merit and opined that the petitioner could not prove his case and that the inclusion of the case property was rightly done and in such a situation the same could not be interfered by this Hon'ble Court in writ jurisdiction. He further submits that summons were duly served upon the parties and thus they appeared before the Court of Settlement and the petitioner had knowledge about the next date but he did not appear before the Court of Settlement nor took any steps. Thus, the Court of Settlement had no alternative but no deliver the judgment on merit which should not be interfered and prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 6. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the record. Admittedly, the petitioner filed the application before the Court of Settlement on 8-1-1987, thereafter he appeared before the court regularly. On perusal of the order Nos. 8-10 of the Court of Settlement it appears that the Court of Settlement was not continuing from 28-1-1995 to 26-7-1995 due to the quorum of the court, but the court resumed on 20-7-95, as such, the petitioner could not appear before the court and the Court of Settlement fixed the date and delivered the judgment on 22-7-95 Order Nos. 8, 9 and 10 are the relevant orders which run as follows: 

 7. From the above order sheets it appears that the Court of Settlement was not continuing from 28-1-1995 to 26-7-1995 due to the quorum of the Court and the Court has been resumed on 20-7-1995 but we do not find any evidence that the parties were duly summoned after reconstituting the Court. 

 8. Section 10 of the Ordinance 54 of 1985 provides that for disposal of the case the Court of Settlement should have followed the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court of Settlement was not in session due to the quorum of the Court for some period and when it was constituted and restarted which amounts to transfer of the court. Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure runs as follows: 

 9. From the above section it appears that when the suit was transferred otherwise an application of the party the court shall then issue notice to the parties but in the instant case the parties were not informed to appear before the court when the court resumed after reconstitution, It further appears that the Court of Settlement opined that the case is barred by limitation but we find that the gazette notification was published on 23-9-1986 and the limitation was for 108 days; the petitioner tiled the case on 8-1-1987 within 107 days which is within due time and, as such, it appears that the finding made by the Court of Settlement fully miscalculated and misread the fact of limitation, inasmuch as the court did not apply its judicial mind. In the case of Bangladesh vs Nasima Khatoon reported in 57 DLR (AD) 97 it has been held that it appears the Court of Settlement did not consider the documents filed by the respondents. While passing the judgment and order it did not apply its Judicial mind. In this view, the judgment passed by the Court of Settlement is not maintainable, and in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Hafizur Rahman reported in 53 DLR (AD) 99 it has been held the "the Court of Settlement did not dispose of the application on merit which it is required to do under the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 and instead, dismissed the application as the respondents were not present in the Court. By not deciding the case on merit the Court of Settlement acted illegally and without lawful authority." 

 10. Admittedly, the Court of Settlement was not in session due to quorum for some period and when it was resumed after due reconstitution the petitioner had reasonable expectation that he should be informed, but it was not done. Consequently, the petitioner could not appear before the court when the matter was taken up for hearing and in such a situation we have no alternative but to interfere with the judgment and order passed by the Court of Settlement. 

 11. The Court of Settlement ought to have given an opportunity to the parties to hear the matter by serving notice upon them but it was not done by the Court of Settlement. So, we are inclined to send back and remand the case to the 1st Court of Settlement to hear the matter on merit after due service of notice upon the parties. 

 12. Considering the facts and circumstance of the case and the discussion made above, it is our considered view that the judgment and order passed by the Court of Settlement is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 22-7-1995 (Annexure-"E" to the writ petition) passed by the 1st Court of Settlement Segunbagicha, Dhaka in Settlement Case No. 9 of 1992 is declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The case is hereby sent back on remand to the 1st Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha; Dhaka for disposal of the same in accordance with law after due service of notice upon the parties. 

 14. Since this is a long pending case, the 1st Court of Settlement Segunbagicha Dhaka is directed to dispose of the matter as early as possible preferably within six months from the date of receipt of the judgment. The petitioner is permitted to take back the original document filed before this court by replacing the attested photostat of the same.
